office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, labor law and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Republican Rep. Deb Manjarrez, a Wapato CPA and orchardist, faces Democrat Ezequiel Morfin, a Toppenish electrician and former city council member. They split on taxes and spending, farmworker collective bargaining, data centers and state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

candidates.summary: One-term State Representative, CPA and Wapato orchardist running on limiting state spending, tighter grant audits and redirecting Climate Commitment Act revenue.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O, services and transportation revenue bills [S5][S6][S7][S8]
Wants tighter grant auditing and accounting standards [S17]
Supports data centers and doubts the Legislature should regulate them [S16]
Voted against the 2025 amendments to the parental-rights law and wrote in support of parents' record-access and notification rights [S9][S19]

taxes.basis: No votes on ESSB 6346, ESHB 2081, ESSB 5814 and ESSB 5801; co-wrote that she stood against 'aggressive new taxes'.

spending.basis: Runs on fighting runaway government spending and tighter grant audits; voted no on the 2025 operating budget.

climate.basis: Blames the 'green agenda' and Climate Commitment Act for utility and fuel costs and voted against the clean fuels bill, but proposes redirecting CCA revenue rather than repeal.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 limits on rent and fee increases; attributes homelessness to drugs and mental illness rather than economics.

safety.basis: Frames homelessness as drug and mental illness, wants children kept from drug-addicted parents, and opposed new firearm requirements; she also sponsored an overdose-mapping bill.

immigration.basis: Voted twice against the 2026 immigrant worker protections bill; no statement on immigration found.

tech.basis: Supports data centers, opposes a 'knee-jerk' ban and is not sure the Legislature should act.

social.basis: Voted against the 2026 bill improving access to abortion medications; no statement found.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296 and co-wrote that she fought for parents' access to records, review of materials and notifications.

experience.basis: One House term, two terms as county Republican chair and 16 years as a precinct committee officer, against a former city council member.

candidates.summary: Toppenish electrician, Yakama Nation electrical inspector and former city council member running on affordability, farmworker collective bargaining and protection of immigrant families.
highlights: Would limit state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement [S3]
Calls farmworker collective bargaining his "largest work" [S5]
Opposes data centers until there is more research [S5]
Supports renter protections, down-payment relief and "fair taxation" [S3][S6]

taxes.basis: Supports 'fair taxation so working people aren't carrying the load alone' and says tax systems favor those at the top; no specific revenue proposal.

spending.basis: Supports $2 billion more for schools and more funding for childcare and preschool.

housing.basis: Would work on renter protections and down-payment relief, alongside tiny homes and expanded city boundaries.

immigration.basis: Supports state protections limiting cooperation with federal immigration enforcement; repeatedly criticizes federal enforcement.

tech.basis: Says no to data centers pending more research and wants oversight and community investment from builders.

experience.basis: Former Toppenish council member and planning commissioner making a first run for the Legislature against an incumbent.
